text.p: England coach Jack Rowell has shrugged off the latest attack on his style of management after being accused by former team supremo Geoff Cooke of talking "mumbo-jumbo".
England open their Five Nations campaign against Scotland at Twickenham on Saturday amid claims from Cooke that the team's modest recent form is the fault of Rowell confusing his players.
"When I left I felt Jack was the right man for the job. But clearly it isn't working," Cooke told a Welsh-based newspaper on Tuesday.
"The biggest problem is that rhetoric off the field has not been matched by performances on it.
"If Jack had shut up and stopped talking all this 'mumbo- jumbo' about interactive rugby and expansive rugby, it would not have created all this weight of expectation.
"The message I am getting is that the players don't know what is expected of them. Communication is not great."

Rowell, a highly successful club coach with Bath before taking the England job in the build-up to the 1995 Rugby World Cup, is clearly losing his patience with his critics, some of whom appear to be operating from within the Rugby Football Union.

"I don't get involved in that type of thing. I don't read this stuff and I don't want to hear about it," said Rowell. "It is interesting though, isn't it? Teams I've coached have won something every year except one since 1984. That's what I call mumbo-jumbo.
"I don't go around criticising coaches or teams or players, it's not me.

"We have made 10 changes in two years which is a huge amount for any team, particularly England. We all aspire to win the Five Nations this season, but it depends how fast the people coming in settle down."
Rowell had to endure a similar attack in November before England's first test of the season against Italy when his predecessor Dick Best claimed he would be sacked at the end of the season.
Best argued that Rowell had wasted a year in shaping a new England side by continuing to pick older players at the expense of developing a new young side.
England, who scraped past Argentina in their last outing last month, had their preparations further complicated on Tuesday when four forwards were unable to train.

Reserves Ben Clarke and Phil Greening reported sick with flu, prop Jason Leonard is still recovering from a minor operation and Martin Johnson injured an ankle playing for Leicester against Brive in last weekend's European Cup final.
